candidates.rationale: Paul encourages believers not to grow weary in doing good, promising a harvest in due season if they don't give up—directly addressing perseverance through extended effort.
The author urges running the race with endurance, fixing eyes on Jesus who endured the cross, providing both example and motivation for long-haul perseverance.
Paul describes forgetting what lies behind and straining toward what is ahead, pressing on toward the goal—a sustained, forward-focused effort over time.
Paul concludes by telling believers to stand firm and give themselves fully to the work, knowing their labor is not in vain—encouragement for steadfast effort when outcomes aren't immediate.
James pronounces a blessing on those who persevere under trial, promising the crown of life to those who remain steadfast—affirming the value of endurance through prolonged difficulty.
